text:
alex: heads-up — seeing intermittent apiserver p99 spikes in eu-west1 coincident with a GPU pool scale-up window. dashboards show apiserver serve_latency spiking to ~2s for list/watch.
jin: saw similar earlier. any ETCD alerts?
maria: yes, etcd leader shows IO stall around the same time. iops and fsync latency up.
alex: attaching quick snippets from the timeline: 
```
2026-03-17T22:10:03Z apiserver p99 2.1s
2026-03-17T22:10:05Z etcd_disk_write_latency 120ms
2026-03-17T22:10:06Z controller-manager lease renew error: context deadline exceeded
```
jin: can you run `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o wide` and paste etcd CPU/io?
maria: i ran it, one etcd host had a transient iops saturation on nvme (~94% util) during the provisioning burst.
tara: db compaction recently bumped because one of the backup jobs got delayed, that increased write amplification. i wonder if compaction/gc + sudden kubelet churn from GPU nodes caused the spike.
alex: that fits. GPU workers booting -> kubelet registering lots of pods -> controller-manager list/watch pressure -> apiserver fanout -> etcd writes and lease pressure.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-ev-92 (apiserver p99 spike eu-west1) :rotating_light:
jin: immediate mitigation options:
- throttle GPU pool scale-ups (rate-limit cluster autoscaler bursts)
- pause scheduled compaction/maintenance jobs for 15m
- add a short-lived apiserver-side cache for heavy list endpoints (if feasible)
- move control-plane disks to higher iops tier for hotfix (if infra change allowed)

maria: i'm going to throttle the autoscaler via the pool config. patch ready:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gpu-pool-ca
spec:
  scaleDownDelay: 10m
  maxScaleUpRate: 5 # reduce burst
```
alex: nice. tara can you delay the compaction/backup that kicked off around 22:08?
tara: delaying compaction now, will reschedule after the window.
jin: while we throttle, we should also lower controller-manager's leader-elect leaseDuration to avoid long waits? careful — too low increases churn. maybe increase `--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period`? unsure.
maria: quick patch we can do: increase etcd io-slo-burst buffer (we use gpustorage? talk to infra). but infra change needs approval.
alex: short action list:
1) maria throttles CA — done (maria)
2) tara delays compaction — in progress (tara)
3) jin to add temporary apiserver flag to increase watch cache size (jin)
4) alex to monitor dashboards and rollback if needed (alex)

jin: for visibility I'm adding a short kube-apiserver log filter to catch 'too many requests' and lease failures and posting counts to the incident.
maria: rolling metrics look better already (p99 down from 2.1s -> 450ms after throttle).
alex: excellent. propose we also add a postmortem action to:
- add autoscaler burst guardrails for all GPU pools
- add control-plane IO SLA check before large batch provisioning
- tune etcd compaction schedule to avoid overlapping with infra-scale events

tara: +1. we should also add a cost note — delayed compaction increases short-term S3 IO but avoids control-plane outages (ops tradeoff).
alex: thanks all. i'll keep the thread updated. tagging @oncall to keep an eye through the evening. :eyes:
